I can't see the repository and have no tools, so this is from memory of Dispatch (Netflix's open-source incident platform) and I haven't verified it against your code.

- **Which function decides:** I believe the decision sits in the case participant flow in `src/dispatch/case/flows.py`, most likely `case_add_or_reactivate_participant_flow`. For a case without a dedicated channel, it checks whether the person should be added to the thread in the shared channel.
- **Cases opened by hand:** I believe not. A manually opened case has no alert (signal) behind it, so there is no alert definition to carry the setting. The thread-add logic only runs when the case came from a signal.
- **Required mark for alert-raised cases:** I believe the alert definition has to carry a flag that opts its cases into having participants added to the thread. I don't remember the exact field name or value with confidence. My best guess is a boolean set to `True`, and you should check the signal model and the flow's condition to confirm.

Treat the four lines below as best guesses, especially the function name and the mark.

FILE: src/dispatch/case/flows.py
FUNCTION: case_add_or_reactivate_participant_flow
HAND_OPENED: no
REQUIRED_MARK: True
